summary: Every new worktree used to start with no node_modules, so the agent ran npm install and the machine ended up with one full copy per worktree - measured at ~700MB each on the user's Mac across 6 worktrees, with the disk at 94% full. cloneDependencyDirs(sourceRoot, worktreeRoot) now fires in the background, right after a worktree is confirmed to exist on disk, and requests a copy-on-write clone of the source project's root node_modules into the new worktree: `cp -c -R` (APFS clonefile) on macOS, `cp -R --reflink=always` on Linux (btrfs/XFS only - it fails outright on ext4, which is intentional). Any other platform, or any failure on macOS/Linux, does nothing and logs once; there is deliberately no full-copy fallback, because that would silently make the disk-space problem worse. The clone never blocks or fails worktree creation: it is fire-and-forget, wrapped so it can never throw into its caller, and a failed clone removes its own partial destination. Wired into every place that runs `git worktree add` for a project: the three flows in src/main/worktree.ts (kanban card, fork-from-message, session - kept for back-compat/tests even though production traffic has moved off them), plus the two call sites that actually run in production today, ExecFileGitWorktreeAdapter.materialize (kanban card creation and fork-to-worktree, via the atomic WorktreeCreationService) and GitLegacySessionWorktreeMaterializer.materialize (new-session-in-worktree-mode, despite the 'legacy' file name). Opt-out via the existing generic settings table: worktree.cloneDependencies = 'false' disables it; unset or any other value means on. The setting is read only once there is actually something to clone (source has node_modules, destination doesn't), so the common no-op case never touches the settings DB.

reactNativeIos.reason: The mobile app is a thin client over WsTransport/IapTransport to a backend host; it never runs git, npm, or a filesystem clone locally and has no node_modules of its own. Worktree creation, and now the dependency clone that follows it, happens entirely on whichever backend (desktop Electron main process or the standalone headless server) the phone is paired with. This change is invisible on the wire - no new IPC channel, no new event - so there is nothing for the mobile client to implement.

nativeAndroid.reason: Same reasoning as reactNativeIos: native Android is a thin client with no local git/npm/filesystem-clone concept and no visibility into backend-side worktree materialization.

updateRelease.reason: No wire protocol, package identity, native module, version, or packaging change. This is a background filesystem helper spawned via execFile (no new dependency) inside existing main-process code; nothing here touches update channels or release packaging.

hardware: Measured on the user's Mac (real APFS filesystem, no mocks): ran the real cloneDependencyDirs(sourceRoot, worktreeRoot) against this repo's own live node_modules (934MB by `du -sh`) as the source and a fresh mkdtemp destination via `npx vite-node -c vitest.config.ts`. Result: 6.3s wall clock, `df -k /` unchanged before and after at Gi resolution (12Gi used / 17Gi available both times) despite the destination reporting the full 944MB under `du -sh` - confirming the clone is block-shared (copy-on-write), not a real copy. The scratch destination directory and its throwaway settings DB dir were both removed after the measurement.
notExercised: The Linux (`--reflink=always`) path was exercised only by unit tests with a mocked runner - no real btrfs/XFS filesystem was available to confirm the actual clonefile/reflink behavior or its ext4 hard-failure, on this Mac.
The headless server (src/server, WsHost) was not run end-to-end on a remote Linux VM for this change; the shared code path is exercised by unit tests only, not a live remote worktree creation.

The three creation flows in src/main/worktree.ts (createWorktree, createForkWorktree, createSessionWorktree) are not reachable from any current production IPC handler - production kanban/fork/session worktree creation now goes through ExecFileGitWorktreeAdapter and GitLegacySessionWorktreeMaterializer instead. The clone call was added to all three anyway per the task's explicit instruction and for back-compat if a caller returns, but it has no live traffic today.
